channel: exchange subscription through the local Bell operating company (the station, not the message)
why_tested: the only route by which a household or office could be reached at all
cost_or_effort: UNKNOWN - no channel cost, sales expense or acquisition cost is broken out in the held print
result: 8,133,017 system stations at 1913-12-31, of which 2,717,808 were not directly the registrant's
notes: the registrant's own telephone-traffic revenue was only 12.1 per cent of its income - the channel belonged to the associated companies, not to P2

channel: toll and long-lines message business accepted at the regular toll rate
why_tested: distance was the registrant's own function and the interconnection letter defines where it began
cost_or_effort: no cost per message is printed
result: about 806,000 toll connections a day; toll lines reaching 70,000 places
repeatability: stated as continuous, but no repeatability measure exists
notes: the 50-mile scope line is the clearest in-window definition of what P2 considered its own product

channel: interconnection with independent companies: the independent builds a standard trunk line to the nearest Bell toll board and pays a per-message connection charge
why_tested: to convert competitors into traffic sources and settle a federal conflict at the same time
cost_or_effort: the independent supplies the trunk line at its own cost; the Bell System keeps control of the whole toll circuit
result: toll charge plus 0.10 USD per message to the independent; long-lines business accepted with no connecting charge
repeatability: UNKNOWN; the schedule is an undertaking, not a measured conversion rate
notes: this is the window's only priced channel, and it was agreed under federal pressure - see U.6

channel: sub-license and connection contracts with local, co-operative and rural companies
why_tested: to extend reach without building the last mile at the registrant's own risk
result: 2,717,808 stations operated this way at 1913-12-31, counted INSIDE the system total
notes: the third of the system that was not the system; also the mechanism by which the registrant's reach figure exceeds its own plant

channel: apparatus wholesale: Western Electric selling to customers outside the Bell System
why_tested: manufacture sold beyond captive demand; the 1908 pamphlet says the selling plan was changed under competitive stress
result: 26,851,790 of 77,532,860 in 1913 sales went to other customers (34.4 per cent, derived)
repeatability: UNKNOWN; the only external read is hostile
notes: supplied by the registrant's own print for the dollars and by the pamphlet for the motive; the motive is not adopted
